Widespread Civil Unrest Disrupts Business Operations Across Nigeria

A wave of civil unrest has swept across several major cities in Nigeria, severely disrupting commercial activity and supply chains as the situation continues to unfold. Protesters took to the streets in Lagos, Abuja, and Port Harcourt late Tuesday, demanding political reforms and denouncing widespread economic inequality. The protests, which have at times turned violent, have triggered road closures, curfews, and intermittent internet blackouts, hampering business operations nationwide.

TotalEnergies Marketing Nigoria PLC confirmed Wednesday that its logistics and retail operations have been “significantly affected” by the ongoing unrest. “Our fuel distribution network is operating at reduced capacity due to roadblocks and safety concerns for staff,” said a spokesperson for the company, which operates hundreds of service stations across Nigeria. The company declined to provide specific figures but noted that several depots and stations have temporarily suspended operations.

Other energy, telecommunications, and consumer goods firms also reported delays in deliveries and reduced workforce attendance. A representative of the Nigerian Chamber of Commerce stated, “These disruptions are impacting not just multinationals but also thousands of small businesses, with daily revenue losses estimated in the tens of millions of dollars.”

Analysts warn that prolonged instability could threaten Nigeria’s fragile economic recovery. “Investor confidence is being tested,” said Adekunle Adebayo, senior economist at Lagos-based consultancy WestBridge Partners. “If these disruptions persist, we could see inflationary pressures intensify and GDP growth projections revised downward.”

The government has appealed for calm and promised dialogue, but as of Wednesday afternoon, demonstrations showed little sign of abating. Local unions have called for an emergency meeting to address workers’ safety and compensation demands.

The situation remains highly fluid, with authorities monitoring developments closely.
